RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 25

An all-male panel is not itself evidence of discrimination — in many ministries it reflects who holds senior grades, and such panels appoint women routinely. On its own it proves nothing, and leading with it can make a strong case look weaker.

Your stronger points are concrete: a missing written explanation two weeks on (often a procedural breach of public-sector recruitment rules), and selection criteria that appear to favour a qualification set you may match or exceed.

So: chase the written reasons formally, in writing, citing the relevant policy. Ask what weighting "international project leadership" carried and when it was added. Mention panel composition as context only — and only if the reasons, once given, don't hold up.
